research_mode: official ONS primary statistical bulletin only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, candidate value, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.name: Release date
verified_claims: The statistical bulletin was released on 23 July 2026.
limitations: Release timing does not make the figures parcel-level or real-time.

sources.name: CSEW headline crime total
verified_claims: The year ending March 2026 Crime Survey for England and Wales estimated 9.6 million incidents of headline crime, with no statistically significant annual change.
limitations: Survey estimates have sampling uncertainty and do not identify exact addresses.

sources.name: CSEW headline crime long-term comparison
verified_claims: CSEW headline crime was 14% lower than in the year ending March 2017.
limitations: The comparison begins when fraud and computer misuse were included in the headline measure.

sources.name: Police recorded crime total
verified_claims: Police recorded around 5.2 million crimes excluding fraud and computer misuse, 1% fewer than the previous year.
limitations: Recorded crime is affected by reporting, recording practice and police activity.

sources.name: Homicide count
verified_claims: Police recorded 499 homicide offences, 7% fewer than the previous year.
limitations: National homicide counts cannot be assigned to a parcel without separate exact-location evidence.

sources.name: Homicide rate
verified_claims: The homicide rate was 8.1 per million people, down from 8.9 per million.
limitations: A national population rate is not a local or parcel risk probability.

sources.name: Knife or sharp instrument homicide
verified_claims: Knife or sharp instrument homicides fell 14% to 176 offences.
limitations: Weapon-category counts are national aggregates and do not establish local exposure.

sources.name: Knife-enabled crime total
verified_claims: Knife-enabled crime recorded by police fell 8% to 48,774 offences.
limitations: By March 2026, 41 forces had switched to the NDQIS identification method, affecting comparability.

sources.name: Knife-enabled offence mix
verified_claims: Assault with injury or intent accounted for 44% and robbery for 39% of knife-enabled crimes.
limitations: The shares describe offence composition, not severity or parcel-level safety.

sources.name: Firearms offence total
verified_claims: Police recorded 5,151 offences involving firearms, 8% fewer than the previous year.
limitations: The measure excludes conventional air weapons and British Transport Police.

sources.name: Firearms type mix
verified_claims: Imitation firearms accounted for 38% and handguns for 31% of recorded firearms offences.
limitations: Weapon-type shares do not locate incidents or identify affected properties.

sources.name: Violence survey estimate
verified_claims: People aged 16 years and over experienced an estimated 989,000 incidents of violence with or without injury, with no statistically significant annual change.
limitations: The estimate is survey-based and excludes children from the respondent population.

sources.name: Violence by perpetrator relationship
verified_claims: About 0.7% reported stranger violence and 0.4% reported acquaintance violence.
limitations: Prevalence percentages are population estimates, not exact-area indicators.

sources.name: Domestic-abuse-related recorded offences
verified_claims: Police categorised 834,256 offences as domestic-abuse-related, including 643,061 violence-against-the-person offences.
limitations: Police data do not measure domestic-abuse prevalence and are affected by recording practices.

sources.name: Sexual victimisation survey estimate
verified_claims: An estimated 2.1% of people aged 16 years and over, around 1 million people, experienced sexual victimisation including attempts.
limitations: New survey questions mean the estimate is not comparable with previously published measures.

sources.name: Police recorded sexual offences
verified_claims: Police recorded 217,567 sexual offences, 4% more than the previous year.
limitations: Recorded trends reflect reporting and recording changes as well as underlying incidents.

sources.name: Robbery of personal property
verified_claims: Robbery of personal property fell 9% to 57,693 offences.
limitations: Police data are preferred for robbery but remain subject to recording changes.

sources.name: Overall robbery
verified_claims: Overall robbery rose 10% to 87,362 offences, mainly because of improved recording of robbery of business property.
limitations: The increase should not be read as a like-for-like rise in personal robbery.

sources.name: CSEW theft estimate
verified_claims: The CSEW estimated 2.6 million theft incidents, with no statistically significant annual change and 29% fewer than a decade earlier.
limitations: Survey theft covers several offence types and is not an exact property register.

sources.name: Vehicle offences
verified_claims: Police recorded vehicle offences fell 11% to 312,250.
limitations: Recorded vehicle crime does not identify parcel exposure without local geospatial evidence.

sources.name: Burglary offences
verified_claims: Police recorded burglary fell 9% to 223,456 offences.
limitations: The figure combines residential and non-residential burglary.

sources.name: Theft from the person
verified_claims: Police recorded theft from the person fell 20% to 121,161 offences.
limitations: National change does not establish neighbourhood or parcel conditions.

sources.name: Shoplifting offences
verified_claims: Police recorded shoplifting fell 4% to 507,086 offences.
limitations: Reporting rates are known to be low and police-retailer engagement can affect recorded levels.

sources.name: Criminal damage survey estimate
verified_claims: The CSEW estimated around 646,000 criminal-damage incidents, with no statistically significant annual change and 47% fewer than a decade earlier.
limitations: Survey uncertainty and broad offence coverage prevent exact parcel attribution.

sources.name: Fraud survey estimate
verified_claims: The CSEW estimated 4.5 million fraud incidents, with no statistically significant annual change; prevalence rose to 7.8%.
limitations: Fraud is generally not a location-based parcel safety measure.

sources.name: Bank and credit account fraud
verified_claims: Bank and credit account fraud increased 15% to around 2.8 million incidents.
limitations: Financial fraud should not be merged into physical-area crime scores without a justified model.

sources.name: Computer misuse survey estimate
verified_claims: The CSEW estimated 798,000 computer-misuse incidents, with no statistically significant annual change and 55% fewer than in the year ending March 2017.
limitations: Cyber incidents are not parcel-located and police-recorded cybercrime was temporarily omitted.

sources.name: Anti-social behaviour survey estimate
verified_claims: An estimated 40.9% experienced or witnessed anti-social behaviour, up from 35.5%.
limitations: The increase was inflated by changes to survey question wording from April 2025.

sources.name: Police-recorded anti-social behaviour
verified_claims: Police-recorded anti-social behaviour incidents remained similar at around 1 million.
limitations: Inspectorate findings indicate some forces need to improve identification and recording.

sources.name: Police data coverage and snapshot
verified_claims: Police recorded crime data cover 43 territorial forces plus British Transport Police and were extracted as a snapshot on 8 June 2026.
limitations: A publication snapshot can be revised and does not provide exact incident coordinates.
